answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded random walks, so influence can wander only a limited distance from independently rooted identities. A sybil cluster may build a summit of mutual endorsements, but its sparse external cut gives it low conductance; min-cut and transitivity bounds limit how much walk probability can enter it. Even when each attestation is authenticated by a cipher-based signature, these spectral limits mathematically cap the cluster’s aggregate voting weight.
